name: Squarespace
verdict: Squarespace reviews every OAuth client registration before issuing credentials, with no stated timeline. A per-site API key skips approval but serves one site and needs a Commerce Advanced plan.
needGuide: Yes — register the OAuth client first and wait for review; nothing works for customers until credentials arrive.

auth.detail: Authorization code flow: GET /authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state (add access_type=offline for a refresh token); the code is valid for 2 minutes and single-use; exchange at POST /tokens. Access tokens last 30 minutes; refresh tokens last 7 days and are single-use (a new one is returned on each refresh). Separate per-site API keys exist for single-site custom apps.

effort.timeToFirstTest: 1-2 hours after credentials are issued; credentials wait is unknown
effort.timeToProduction: unknown (approval of the client registration has no stated SLA)

approval.gate: Squarespace reviews every OAuth client registration before issuing credentials (no timeline given beyond 'as soon as possible'). The docs say OAuth is for Squarespace Extensions. The Commerce APIs-only API-key path needs no approval but only serves one site and needs a Commerce Advanced plan.

scopes.why: A short list of website.* scopes with .read variants; no scope-specific review documented.
scopes.summary: Scopes: website.orders, website.transactions.read, website.inventory, website.products, website.contacts, website.discounts, each with a .read variant. No scope-specific review was documented.

cost: OAuth: no fee documented. API keys: site must be on Commerce Advanced plan.
prerequisites: Account and owner: A company-owned Squarespace account to hold the developer app registration.

Where you register: Log in at account.squarespace.com → Developer Apps → register an OAuth client: client name, 1:1 .png/.svg icon (max 200 KB), redirect URIs, terms and privacy links. Squarespace reviews it, then issues client ID and secret.
Cost: OAuth: no fee documented. API keys: site must be on Commerce Advanced plan.

registerAt.path: Log in at account.squarespace.com → Developer Apps → register an OAuth client: client name, 1:1 .png/.svg icon (max 200 KB), redirect URIs, terms and privacy links. Squarespace reviews it, then issues client ID and secret.

steps.do: Prepare icon, privacy policy and terms pages, and HTTPS redirect URIs
Register the OAuth client at account.squarespace.com/developer-apps and wait for review
Meanwhile prototype with a per-site API key on your own Commerce Advanced site
Implement authorize redirect with state, code exchange at POST /tokens, and offline access
Implement refresh with single-use rotation, storing the latest refresh token, refreshing before 30-minute expiry and at least weekly
Handle 401 by asking the user to reconnect; test deny and revoke paths
Subscribe to webhooks through the Webhook Subscriptions API (OAuth only)

roles.team: A company-owned Squarespace account to hold the developer app registration.
roles.customer: The site owner or a user allowed to connect extensions approves the consent screen; they can revoke it in Squarespace later, which invalidates tokens.

testing: Use a Squarespace trial or test site with Commerce data once your client is approved, and a second site to test the multi-site case.
API keys (Settings → Advanced → Developer API Keys) can test endpoints on your own site before OAuth approval.

blockers.fix: A connection idle for more than a week needs re-consent, so schedule refreshes.
Persist atomically or concurrent refreshes lock you out.
Submit early and have a per-site API key fallback for single customers.
Exchange immediately and URL-decode before sending.

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth client and token-rotation code, draft registration copy and privacy/terms pages, and run API test calls.
automation.humanMust: Register the client while logged in, wait for approval, and have the site owner approve the consent screen.

uncertain: Whether unlisted extensions or only Extension Directory partners are approved, approval timeline, and whether Commerce plan is needed on customer sites for OAuth were not confirmed.
The authentication page said OAuth works on any plan.
